english: do unto others as you would have them do unto you
also: do as you would be done by

terms.latin: Ab aliō exspectēs alterī quod fēceris.
terms.comment: Literally “you may expect from another what you have done to someone else”. We have found no ancient source for it in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
